sanskrit: kīrtitā draupadī vācā anujñātā ca pāṇḍavaiḥ bhavaty avijitā kena hetunaiṣā matā tava
english: Draupadī has been named aloud and released by the Pāṇḍavas themselves — on what ground then do you hold that she is not conquered?

sanskrit: manyase vā sabhām etām ānītām ekavāsasam adharmeṇeti tatrāpi śṛṇu me vākyam uttaram
english: Or do you think that bringing her into this assembly in a single garment was an act of unrighteousness? Hear my further word on that point as well.

sanskrit: eko bhartā striyā devair vihitaḥ kurunandana iyaṃ tv anekavaśagā bandhakīti viniścitā
english: The gods have ordained that a woman shall have one husband, O delight of the Kurus; but this one is subject to many masters — she is therefore rightly judged a harlot.

sanskrit: asyāḥ sabhām ānayanaṃ na citram iti me matiḥ ekāmbaradharatvaṃ vāpy atha vāpi vivastratā
english: In my opinion it is no wonder that she has been brought into the hall, nor that she is clad in a single garment, nor even that she should be stripped bare.

sanskrit: yac caiṣāṃ draviṇaṃ kiṃ cid yā caiṣā ye ca pāṇḍavāḥ saubaleneha tat sarvaṃ dharmeṇa vijitaṃ vasu
english: Whatever wealth belongs to them, and this woman herself, and the Pāṇḍavas — all that property has been lawfully won here by the son of Subala.

sanskrit: duḥśāsana subālo 'yaṃ vikarṇaḥ prājñavādikaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca vāsāṃsi draupadyāś cāpy upāhara
english: Duḥśāsana, this Vikarṇa is but a boy playing the wise man — bring in the garments of the Pāṇḍavas and of Draupadī too.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā pāṇḍavāḥ sarve svāni vāsāṃsi bhārata avakīryottarīyāṇi sabhāyāṃ samupāviśan
english: Hearing that, O Bhārata, all the Pāṇḍavas cast off their upper garments and sat down in the assembly.

sanskrit: tato duḥśāsano rājan draupadyā vasanaṃ balāt sabhāmadhye samākṣipya vyapakraṣṭuṃ pracakrame
english: Then Duḥśāsana, O king, seized Draupadī's garment by force in the middle of the assembly and began to strip it off.

sanskrit: ākṛṣyamāṇe vasane draupadyās tu viśāṃ pate tadrūpam aparaṃ vastraṃ prādurāsīd anekaśaḥ
english: As Draupadī's garment was being pulled away, O lord of the people, another robe of the same kind appeared, and then another, and yet another, in endless succession.

sanskrit: tato halahalāśabdas tatrāsīd ghoranisvanaḥ tad adbhutatamaṃ loke vīkṣya sarvamahīkṣitām
english: Then a loud and terrible cry of amazement arose there as all the assembled kings witnessed that most wondrous marvel in the world.

sanskrit: śaśāpa tatra bhīmas tu rājamadhye mahāsvanaḥ krodhād visphuramāṇoṣṭho viniṣpiṣya kare karam
english: Then Bhīma, in the midst of the kings, with a great roar, his lips quivering with rage and grinding palm against palm, uttered a curse.

sanskrit: idaṃ me vākyam ādaddhvaṃ kṣatriyā lokavāsinaḥ noktapūrvaṃ narair anyair na cānyo yad vadiṣyati
english: "Hear this my vow, all you Kṣatriyas who dwell in this world — a vow never spoken before by any man, nor shall another ever speak it:

sanskrit: yady etad evam uktvā tu na kuryāṃ pṛthivīśvarāḥ pitāmahānāṃ sarveṣāṃ nāhaṃ gatim avāpnuyām
english: If, having spoken thus, I do not carry it out, O lords of the earth, then may I not attain the path of all our forefathers.

sanskrit: asya pāpasya durjāter bhāratāpasadasya ca na pibeyaṃ balād vakṣo bhittvā ced rudhiraṃ yudhi
english: If in battle I do not split open the chest of this vile, low-born disgrace to the Bharatas by force and drink his blood —

sanskrit: tasya te vacanaṃ śrutvā sarvalokapraharṣaṇam pracakrur bahulāṃ pūjāṃ kutsanto dhṛtarāṣṭrajam
english: Hearing those words of his, which thrilled all the world with joy, the assembly gave him great honor while denouncing the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: yadā tu vāsasāṃ rāśiḥ sabhāmadhye samācitaḥ tato duḥśāsanaḥ śrānto vrīḍitaḥ samupāviśat
english: When a heap of garments had accumulated in the middle of the assembly, Duḥśāsana at last, exhausted and ashamed, sat down.

sanskrit: dhikśabdas tu tatas tatra samabhūl lomaharṣaṇaḥ sabhyānāṃ naradevānāṃ dṛṣṭvā kuntīsutāṃs tadā
english: Then a hair-raising cry of "Shame!" arose among the assembled god-like men as they looked upon the sons of Kuntī.

sanskrit: na vibruvanti kauravyāḥ praśnam etam iti sma ha sa janaḥ krośati smātra dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ vigarhayan
english: "The Kurus will not answer this question" — so the people there cried out, denouncing Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: tato bāhū samucchritya nivārya ca sabhāsadaḥ viduraḥ sarvadharmajña idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then Vidura, knower of all dharma, raised both arms high to silence the assembly and spoke these words:

sanskrit: vidura uvāca draupadī praśnam uktvaivaṃ roravīti hy anāthavat na ca vibrūta taṃ praśnaṃ sabhyā dharmo 'tra pīḍyate
english: Vidura said: "Draupadī has posed her question and is crying like one without a protector, yet you assembled members do not answer that question — dharma is being wounded here."

sanskrit: sabhāṃ prapadyate hy ārtaḥ prajvalann iva havyavāṭ taṃ vai satyena dharmeṇa sabhyāḥ praśamayanty uta
english: "For one in distress enters an assembly blazing like fire, and it is the duty of the assembled members to pacify that person with truth and with dharma.

sanskrit: dharmapraśnam atho brūyād ārtaḥ sabhyeṣu mānavaḥ vibrūyus tatra te praśnaṃ kāmakrodhavaśātigāḥ
english: "When a person in distress poses a question of dharma to the members of an assembly, those members, who have transcended the sway of desire and anger, should answer that question.

sanskrit: vikarṇena yathāprajñam uktaḥ praśno narādhipāḥ bhavanto 'pi hi taṃ praśnaṃ vibruvantu yathāmati
english: "The question has been answered by Vikarṇa to the best of his wisdom, O kings — let you too answer that question as your minds direct.

sanskrit: yo hi praśnaṃ na vibrūyād dharmadarśī sabhāṃ gataḥ anṛte yā phalāvāptis tasyāḥ so 'rdhaṃ samaśnute
english: "For a man who, though seeing what is right, enters an assembly and does not answer a question, reaps one half of the fruit that accrues from falsehood.

sanskrit: yaḥ punar vitathaṃ brūyād dharmadarśī sabhāṃ gataḥ anṛtasya phalaṃ kṛtsnaṃ saṃprāpnotīti niścayaḥ
english: "And he who, though seeing what is right, enters an assembly and gives a false answer — he obtains the entire fruit of untruth: this is certain.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam prahlādasya ca saṃvādaṃ muner āṅgirasasya ca
english: "On this point they cite this ancient tale — the dialogue between Prahlāda and the sage of the Āṅgirasa line.

sanskrit: prahlādo nāma daityendras tasya putro virocanaḥ kanyāhetor āṅgirasaṃ sudhanvānam upādravat
english: "There was a lord of the Daityas named Prahlāda; his son was Virocana. For the sake of a maiden Virocana challenged Sudhanvan, the descendant of Āṅgiras.

sanskrit: ahaṃ jyāyān ahaṃ jyāyān iti kanyepsayā tadā tayor devanam atrāsīt prāṇayor iti naḥ śrutam
english: "Each claiming 'I am the superior one, I am the superior one,' both of them, desiring the maiden, staked their very lives in a wager — so we have heard.

sanskrit: tayoḥ praśnavivādo 'bhūt prahlādaṃ tāv apṛcchatām jyāyān ka āvayor ekaḥ praśnaṃ prabrūhi mā mṛṣā
english: "A dispute over this question arose between them, and they both went to Prahlāda and asked him: 'Tell us truly — which of us two is the superior? Answer the question and do not lie.'

sanskrit: sa vai vivadanād bhītaḥ sudhanvānaṃ vyalokayat taṃ sudhanvābravīt kruddho brahmadaṇḍa iva jvalan
english: "Fearing to pronounce in the dispute, Prahlāda glanced sideways at Sudhanvan. Sudhanvan, enraged and blazing like the rod of Brahmā, spoke to him:

sanskrit: yadi vai vakṣyasi mṛṣā prahlādātha na vakṣyasi śatadhā te śiro vajrī vajreṇa prahariṣyati
english: "'If you speak falsely, Prahlāda, or if you refuse to speak at all, the Thunderer will shatter your head into a hundred pieces with his vajra.'

sanskrit: sudhanvanā tathoktaḥ san vyathito 'śvatthaparṇavat jagāma kaśyapaṃ daityaḥ paripraṣṭuṃ mahaujasam
english: "Thus threatened by Sudhanvan, the Daitya trembled like a leaf of the aśvattha tree and went to the mighty Kaśyapa to inquire further of him.

sanskrit: prahlāda uvāca tvaṃ vai dharmasya vijñātā daivasyehāsurasya ca brāhmaṇasya mahāprājña dharmakṛcchram idaṃ śṛṇu
english: "Prahlāda said: 'You are the knower of dharma here — of the divine, the demonic, and the brahminical. O greatly wise one, hear this dilemma of dharma.'

sanskrit: yo vai praśnaṃ na vibrūyād vitathaṃ vāpi nirdiśet ke vai tasya pare lokās tan mamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ
english: "'Tell me, I ask you: what are the other worlds — the afterlife — of one who neither answers a question nor directs it falsely?'

sanskrit: kaśyapa uvāca jānan na vibruvan praśnaṃ kāmāt krodhāt tathā bhayāt sahasraṃ vāruṇān pāśān ātmani pratimuñcati
english: "Kaśyapa said: 'One who knows and yet, out of desire, anger, or fear, does not answer a question, binds upon himself a thousand nooses of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: tasya saṃvatsare pūrṇe pāśa ekaḥ pramucyate tasmāt satyaṃ tu vaktavyaṃ jānatā satyam añjasā
english: "'At the end of each full year one noose is released; therefore one who knows the truth must speak the truth plainly and directly.'

sanskrit: viddho dharmo hy adharmeṇa sabhāṃ yatra prapadyate na cāsya śalyaṃ kṛntanti viddhās tatra sabhāsadaḥ
english: "Where dharma, pierced by adharma, enters an assembly and the assembled members, who are themselves wounded by it, do not remove its thorn —

sanskrit: ardhaṃ harati vai śreṣṭhaḥ pādo bhavati kartṛṣu pādaś caiva sabhāsatsu ye na nindanti ninditam
english: "— the chief man there carries off one half of the sin; one quarter falls upon those who committed the deed; one quarter falls upon the members of the assembly who do not condemn what deserves condemnation.

sanskrit: anenā bhavati śreṣṭho mucyante ca sabhāsadaḥ eno gacchati kartāraṃ nindārho yatra nindyate
english: "But where the one deserving condemnation is duly condemned, the chief man is freed from sin and so are the members of the assembly — the guilt goes entirely to the doer.

sanskrit: vitathaṃ tu vadeyur ye dharmaṃ prahlāda pṛcchate iṣṭāpūrtaṃ ca te ghnanti sapta caiva parāvarān
english: "Those who, when asked about dharma, O Prahlāda, answer falsely — they destroy both the merit of their rituals and charitable works and seven generations of their ancestors and descendants alike.'

sanskrit: hṛtasvasya hi yad duḥkhaṃ hataputrasya cāpi yat ṛṇinaṃ prati yac caiva rājñā grastasya cāpi yat
english: "The anguish of one whose wealth has been plundered, the anguish of one whose son has been slain, the anguish of one crushed by debt, and the anguish of one seized by the king —

sanskrit: striyāḥ patyā vihīnāyāḥ sārthād bhraṣṭasya caiva yat adhyūḍhāyāś ca yad duḥkhaṃ sākṣibhir vihatasya ca
english: "— the anguish of a woman bereft of her husband, the anguish of one separated from a caravan, the anguish of one whose marriage has been supplanted, and the anguish of one ruined by witnesses —

sanskrit: etāni vai samāny āhur duḥkhāni tridaśeśvarāḥ tāni sarvāṇi duḥkhāni prāpnoti vitathaṃ bruvan
english: "— all these sorrows the lords of the thirty gods declare to be equal to one another; and all those sorrows does one incur who speaks falsely.

sanskrit: samakṣadarśanāt sākṣyaṃ śravaṇāc ceti dhāraṇāt tasmāt satyaṃ bruvan sākṣī dharmārthābhyāṃ na hīyate
english: "Testimony comes from direct sight, from hearing, and from firm memory. Therefore a witness who speaks the truth suffers no loss in either dharma or worldly welfare.'

sanskrit: vidura uvāca kaśyapasya vacaḥ śrutvā prahlādaḥ putram abravīt śreyān sudhanvā tvatto vai mattaḥ śreyāṃs tathāṅgirāḥ
english: Vidura said: "Having heard Kaśyapa's words, Prahlāda said to his son: 'Sudhanvan is superior to you, and Āṅgiras is superior to me.'

sanskrit: mātā sudhanvanaś cāpi śreyasī mātṛtas tava virocana sudhanvāyaṃ prāṇānām īśvaras tava
english: "'Sudhanvan's mother too is superior to yours in terms of maternal lineage, Virocana — and this Sudhanvan is the master of your very life.'

sanskrit: sudhanvovāca putrasnehaṃ parityajya yas tvaṃ dharme pratiṣṭhitaḥ anujānāmi te putraṃ jīvatv eṣa śataṃ samāḥ
english: Sudhanvan said: "Because you have set aside paternal affection and stood firm in dharma, I grant your son his life — may he live a hundred years."

sanskrit: vidura uvāca evaṃ vai paramaṃ dharmaṃ śrutvā sarve sabhāsadaḥ yathāpraśnaṃ tu kṛṣṇāyā manyadhvaṃ tatra kiṃ param
english: Vidura said: "Having heard this supreme lesson of dharma, all of you members of the assembly — consider now what is the highest answer to Kṛṣṇā's question."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vidurasya vacaḥ śrutvā nocuḥ kiṃ cana pārthivāḥ karṇo duḥśāsanaṃ tv āha kṛṣṇāṃ dāsīṃ gṛhān naya
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: "Having heard Vidura's words, the assembled kings said nothing at all; but Karṇa said to Duḥśāsana: 'Take this slave-woman Kṛṣṇā to the inner apartments.'

sanskrit: tāṃ vepamānāṃ savrīḍāṃ pralapantīṃ sma pāṇḍavān duḥśāsanaḥ sabhāmadhye vicakarṣa tapasvinīm
english: "Duḥśāsana dragged that afflicted woman — trembling, red with shame, calling out to the Pāṇḍavas — through the middle of the assembly.

sanskrit: draupady uvāca purastāt karaṇīyaṃ me na kṛtaṃ kāryam uttaram vihvalāsmi kṛtānena karṣatā balinā balāt
english: Draupadī said: "The duty I should have performed first has not been done, nor the duty due afterward — I am in anguish, dragged by force by this one who has done such a deed."

sanskrit: abhivādaṃ karomy eṣāṃ gurūṇāṃ kurusaṃsadi na me syād aparādho 'yaṃ yad idaṃ na kṛtaṃ mayā
english: "I would offer my reverential salutation to these elders assembled here in the Kuru court — let the fault not be mine that this has not been done by me."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sā tena ca samuddhūtā duḥkhena ca tapasvinī patitā vilalāpedaṃ sabhāyām atathocitā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: "Shaken by that dragging and by her grief, the afflicted one — fallen down, undeserving of such treatment — lamented thus in the assembly."

sanskrit: draupady uvāca svayaṃvare yāsmi nṛpair dṛṣṭā raṅge samāgataiḥ na dṛṣṭapūrvā cānyatra sāham adya sabhāṃ gatā
english: Draupadī said: "I who was seen by the assembled kings at the svayaṃvara arena, and who had never been seen elsewhere — I have today been brought into this assembly."

sanskrit: yāṃ na vāyur na cādityo dṛṣṭavantau purā gṛhe sāham adya sabhāmadhye dṛśyāmi kurusaṃsadi
english: "I whom neither the wind nor the sun had ever seen before in my own home — I am today being seen in the middle of this assembly, in the Kuru court."

sanskrit: yāṃ na mṛṣyanti vātena spṛśyamānāṃ purā gṛhe spṛśyamānāṃ sahante 'dya pāṇḍavās tāṃ durātmanā
english: "I whom the Pāṇḍavas formerly would not suffer to be touched even by the wind in my own home — those same Pāṇḍavas today endure this vile-souled man's touching me."

sanskrit: mṛṣyante kuravaś ceme manye kālasya paryayam snuṣāṃ duhitaraṃ caiva kliśyamānām anarhatīm
english: "These Kurus too endure it — I believe it is the turning of time — that their daughter-in-law and daughter is being afflicted, undeserving of such treatment."

sanskrit: kiṃ tv ataḥ kṛpaṇaṃ bhūyo yad ahaṃ strī satī śubhā sabhāmadhyaṃ vigāhe 'dya kva nu dharmo mahīkṣitām
english: "What could be more pitiable than this — that I, a chaste and virtuous woman, am today plunged into the middle of an assembly? Where now is the dharma of these kings?"

sanskrit: dharmyāḥ striyaḥ sabhāṃ pūrvaṃ na nayantīti naḥ śrutam sa naṣṭaḥ kauraveyeṣu pūrvo dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: "We have heard that virtuous women are not to be brought into an assembly — that primordial and eternal dharma has perished among the Kauravas."

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi bhāryā pāṇḍūnāṃ pārṣatasya svasā satī vāsudevasya ca sakhī pārthivānāṃ sabhām iyām
english: "How could I — wife of the Pāṇḍavas, true sister of Dhṛṣṭadyumna the son of Pṛṣata, and a dear friend of Vāsudeva — come to be brought into this assembly of kings?"

sanskrit: tām imāṃ dharmarājasya bhāryāṃ sadṛśavarṇajām brūta dāsīm adāsīṃ vā tat kariṣyāmi kauravāḥ
english: "Declare me — this wife of Dharmarāja, born of equal class — a slave-woman or a free woman: whichever you declare, that I shall accept, O Kauravas."

sanskrit: ayaṃ hi māṃ dṛḍhaṃ kṣudraḥ kauravāṇāṃ yaśoharaḥ kliśnāti nāhaṃ tat soḍhuṃ ciraṃ śakṣyāmi kauravāḥ
english: "For this vile wretch, the destroyer of the Kauravas' glory, is tormenting me grievously — I cannot bear it much longer, O Kauravas."

sanskrit: jitāṃ vāpy ajitāṃ vāpi manyadhvaṃ vā yathā nṛpāḥ tathā pratyuktam icchāmi tat kariṣyāmi kauravāḥ
english: "Whether you consider me won or not won, O kings — I desire to be answered accordingly, and whatever answer you give, that I shall accept, O Kauravas."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca uktavān asmi kalyāṇi dharmasya tu parāṃ gatim loke na śakyate gantum api viprair mahātmabhiḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: "I have said before, O auspicious one, that the highest course of dharma cannot be pursued in this world even by wise and great-souled men."

sanskrit: balavāṃs tu yathā dharmaṃ loke paśyati pūruṣaḥ sa dharmo dharmavelāyāṃ bhavaty abhihitaḥ paraiḥ
english: "Yet as a powerful man sees dharma in the world, so that dharma, at the moment of dharma's testing, is declared by those who are his equals or superiors."

sanskrit: na vivektuṃ ca te praśnam etaṃ śaknomi niścayāt sūkṣmatvād gahanatvāc ca kāryasyāsya ca gauravāt
english: "I am not able to adjudicate your question with certainty — because of the subtlety and profundity of the matter, and because of the gravity of this situation."

sanskrit: nūnam antaḥ kulasyāsya bhavitā nacirād iva tathā hi kuravaḥ sarve lobhamohaparāyaṇāḥ
english: "Surely the end of this family is not far off — for the Kurus are all given over entirely to greed and delusion."

sanskrit: kuleṣu jātāḥ kalyāṇi vyasanābhyāhatā bhṛśam dharmyān mārgān na cyavante yathā nas tvaṃ vadhūḥ sthitā
english: "Those born in good families, O auspicious one, though assailed by misfortune, do not abandon the paths of dharma — just as you, our daughter-in-law, have steadfastly remained."

sanskrit: upapannaṃ ca pāñcāli tavedaṃ vṛttam īdṛśam yat kṛcchram api saṃprāptā dharmam evānvavekṣase
english: "And this conduct of yours is entirely fitting, O Pāñcālī — that even having fallen into this extremity, you look only to dharma."

sanskrit: ete droṇādayaś caiva vṛddhā dharmavido janāḥ śūnyaiḥ śarīrais tiṣṭhanti gatāsava ivānatāḥ
english: "These elders — Droṇa and the others — who are knowers of dharma, stand here with bodies drained of life, bowed down as though their breath has already departed."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu praśne 'smin pramāṇam iti me matiḥ ajitāṃ vā jitāṃ vāpi svayaṃ vyāhartum arhati
english: "In this question it is my view that Yudhiṣṭhira is the authority — it is for him himself to declare whether she was won or not won."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā tu dṛṣṭvā bahu tat tad evaṃ; rorūyamāṇāṃ kurarīm ivārtām nocur vacaḥ sādhv atha vāpy asādhu; mahīkṣito dhārtarāṣṭrasya bhītāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: "Seeing all of that, the assembled kings, fearful of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, did not speak a word — neither approval nor disapproval — while she wailed like a distressed osprey."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu tān pārthivaputrapautrāṃs; tūṣṇīṃbhūtān dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putraḥ smayann ivedaṃ vacanaṃ babhāṣe; pāñcālarājasya sutāṃ tadānīm
english: "Seeing those sons and grandsons of kings fallen silent, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra at that moment spoke these words with what seemed like a smile, addressing the daughter of the Pāñcāla king:"

sanskrit: tiṣṭhatv ayaṃ praśna udārasattve; bhīme 'rjune sahadeve tathaiva patyau ca te nakule yājñaseni; vadantv ete vacanaṃ tvatprasūtam
english: "'Let this question rest with the noble-natured ones — with Bhīma, with Arjuna, with Sahadeva, and likewise with your husband Nakula, O Yājñasenī — let them speak the word that arises from you.'

sanskrit: anīśvaraṃ vibruvantv āryamadhye; yudhiṣṭhiraṃ tava pāñcāli hetoḥ kurvantu sarve cānṛtaṃ dharmarājaṃ; pāñcāli tvaṃ mokṣyase dāsabhāvāt
english: "'Let them declare in this assembly of the noble that Yudhiṣṭhira has no mastery over you, O Pāñcālī — let them all make Dharmarāja speak falsehood on your account, and Pāñcālī, you shall be freed from the state of bondage.'

sanskrit: dharme sthito dharmarājo mahātmā; svayaṃ cedaṃ kathayatv indrakalpaḥ īśo vā te yady anīśo 'tha vaiṣa; vākyād asya kṣipram ekaṃ bhajasva
english: "'Or let the great-souled Dharmarāja, who stands in dharma, like unto Indra himself — let him declare it himself: is he your master or is he not? Speedily choose one answer from his own words.'

sanskrit: sarve hīme kauraveyāḥ sabhāyāṃ; duḥkhāntare vartamānās tavaiva na vibruvanty āryasattvā yathāvat; patīṃś ca te samavekṣyālpabhāgyān
english: "'For all these Kaurava nobles of virtuous character who are gathered in this assembly, being themselves in the midst of suffering on your account, do not speak as they ought — eyeing your husbands of meager fortune.'"

sanskrit: tataḥ sabhyāḥ kururājasya tatra; vākyaṃ sarve praśaśaṃsus tadoccaiḥ celāvedhāṃś cāpi cakrur nadanto; hā hety āsīd api caivātra nādaḥ sarve cāsan pārthivāḥ prītimantaḥ; kuruśreṣṭhaṃ dhārmikaṃ pūjayantaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: "Thereupon all the members of the Kuru king's assembly loudly praised those words; shouting and throwing their upper garments, a cry of 'Ah! Ah!' rose up there, and all the assembled kings were gladdened, honoring that most righteous one of the Kurus."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraṃ ca te sarve samudaikṣanta pārthivāḥ kiṃ nu vakṣyati dharmajña iti sācīkṛtānanāḥ
english: "And all those kings gazed at Yudhiṣṭhira with faces turned sidelong, thinking: 'What will the knower of dharma now say?'"

sanskrit: kiṃ nu vakṣyati bībhatsur ajito yudhi pāṇḍavaḥ bhīmaseno yamau ceti bhṛśaṃ kautūhalānvitāḥ
english: "'What will Bībhatsu say? What will Ajita, the unconquered Pāṇḍava in battle, say? What will Bhīmasena say, and the twins?' — so they thought, filled with intense curiosity."
